feedback: Written before the complete robot has raced. Iteration 0 has no earlier race outcomes, so this feedback rests only on the public contract and on how the controller was built for this geometry. Integration notes: (1) The five sensors are symmetric about x = 0, so I used antisymmetric weights [-2, -1, 0, 1, 2]. The signal sign follows the contract's left-positive convention. (2) With a 12 mm footprint and 0.02 m spacing, one sensor always sees a graded reading when the line is 1 cm off, so the signal is smooth and no extra filtering is needed. (3) The sensors lead the axle by 0.05 m, so the controller has time to react, but kd is needed to damp the loop; I kept ki at 0 because the integral term would wind up on bends. (4) Wheel track 0.12 m and radius 0.03 m gave enough turn authority at kp 3.0 with no saturation expected. What to change after the next race: if max_error is large and line_loss_events is above 0 on the s-bend or slalom, the sensor lead is probably too long for the bend rate; move sensors toward the axle. If steering_oscillation is high while rms_error is low, the lead is probably fine and the geometry should stay, with more damping in the controller. If the robot completes with small errors, keep the geometry and push speed through the controller.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events > 0 or max_error is above 0.03 m on the s-bend or slalom, reduce the sensor lead by setting every sensor y from 0.05 to 0.03 (keep x positions and sensor_size 0.012), because the lag from a 0.05 m lead on tight bends is the likeliest cause.

If steering_oscillation is high while rms_error stays under about 0.02 m, keep the sensor geometry and ask for wider spacing of 0.024 m (x = -0.048 to +0.048) to make the signal less sensitive to small offsets. This is a geometry test only; no race yet shows it helps.

If the robot completes but completion_time is above 2.5 s, try wheel_track 0.10 m (from 0.12 m) to increase turn rate per PWM difference, so the robot can hold the line at higher base_speed; this is untested and rests only on the contract's turn-rate rule.
